items.title: Alexandre Lebrun passe le flambeau à Brian Manning à la tête de Nabla
items.summary: Alexandre Lebrun has stepped down as head of Nabla, with Brian Manning taking over leadership of the company. The leadership transition was reported by Maddyness.

items.title: Why AMI Labs’ Alexandre LeBrun won’t call his AI ‘AGI’ or ‘superintelligence’
items.summary: AMI Labs founder Alexandre LeBrun avoids labeling his artificial intelligence systems as "AGI" (Artificial General Intelligence) or "superintelligence," preferring more cautious terminology around AI capabilities. The distinction reflects a broader debate in the AI industry about how to responsibly describe and discuss advanced machine intelligence development.

items.title: Why AMI Labs’ Alexandre LeBrun won't call his AI 'AGI' or 'superintelligence' | TechCrunch
items.summary: AMI Labs founder Alexandre LeBrun avoids using terms like "AGI" (Artificial General Intelligence) or "superintelligence" to describe his company's AI systems. The article explores LeBrun's reasoning for rejecting these commonly used labels in the AI industry, suggesting a more cautious or precise approach to characterizing the capabilities of his technology.

headline: LeBrun's Semantic Caution Is the Clearest Signal of AMI's Public Strategy This Week
stateOfPlay: A quiet week on the technical front — no new publications, no new hires, minimal GitHub activity — throws AMI's public positioning into sharper relief. The dominant story is founder Alexandre LeBrun's deliberate refusal to deploy the language of AGI or superintelligence, covered by TechCrunch and amplified via Biztoc. Combined with LeBrun's concurrent exit from the Nabla chairmanship, the week suggests a founder increasingly focused on AMI's identity and narrative as the company's primary asset at this stage. There is no new research or product signal to read this week; the signal is the silence, and what AMI's leadership chooses to say into it.

threads.title: Rejecting 'AGI' Is a Strategic Positioning Move, Not Just Humility
threads.narrative:
LeBrun's explicit refusal to call AMI's systems AGI or superintelligence — reported by TechCrunch on July 16 — is worth reading as deliberate brand architecture, not mere epistemic caution. In a funding environment where competitors race to claim the most expansive capabilities, opting for more precise language carves out a distinct positioning: AMI as the serious, technically grounded alternative to hype-driven labs. This is the same rhetorical territory Yann LeCun has long occupied in public debates about AI progress, and it reinforces the intellectual lineage AMI's co-founding leans on.

The practical effect is to set expectations carefully at a moment when AMI has not yet made major public technical disclosures. With no new papers this week and a thin GitHub footprint, the founder's language choices become the company's loudest output. Framing matters most when the product is not yet visible.

threads.title: The Nabla Departure Frees LeBrun for AMI — and Raises the Stakes
threads.narrative:
The July 22 Maddyness report that LeBrun has handed Nabla's leadership to Brian Manning is a meaningful contextual fact for AMI-watchers. LeBrun co-founded Nabla and has been a central figure there; stepping back now suggests he is consolidating his attention on AMI at a moment when the startup is presumably approaching a critical early phase — whether that means a first product, a funding round, or a research debut.

This is not a distress signal for AMI; it reads as the opposite. Founders typically shed board or operational commitments at other companies when they need bandwidth for an intensive push. The timing, coinciding with a week of public narrative-setting via TechCrunch, points to deliberate preparation rather than coincidence.

threads.title: Pascale Fung's Defence of Industry-Funded Research Signals Team Alignment on a Contested Question
threads.narrative:
AMI team member Pascale Fung posted publicly on July 18 to defend the record of large industry research labs — Bell Labs, IBM, Xerox PARC, Microsoft, Google — as the source of paradigm-changing AI advances, pushing back against critics of industry-funded science. The post drew modest engagement (32 likes, 3 retweets), but its content matters more than its reach.

For a team that includes Yann LeCun and operates at the intersection of deep academic credibility and commercial ambition, this is an implicit self-justification: AMI's model — serious research inside or adjacent to an industry-funded lab — is historically validated. Fung is not speaking for the company, but the stance is consistent with AMI's foundational logic and suggests the team is thinking carefully about how it wants to be perceived within the broader research community.

evidence.label: Pascale Fung on X: defence of industry-funded research

whatToWatch: Whether LeBrun's TechCrunch appearance is a precursor to a more substantive announcement — a funding round, a first product reveal, or a research publication — in the coming weeks. The combination of narrative-setting and the Nabla exit suggests AMI is preparing for a more visible moment; watch for new job postings or a GitHub activity surge as early indicators.
